title: The Story of King Arthur and His Knights

author.name: Howard Pyle
author.biography: Born in Wilmington, Delaware, he wrote four books of Arthurian legend between 1903 and 1910, of which this is the first.

hook.text: What makes a young man nobody has heard of fit to be king?

paragraphs: When King Uther-Pendragon dies, Britain falls into quarrels among its lords, and his infant son has vanished: the enchanter Merlin and Sir Ulfius carried him away by night. Years later Merlin sets a test. A sword appears, fixed in an anvil on a block of marble, and whoever can draw it out will be the rightful King of Britain.
Arthur has been raised as a son of the knight Sir Ector. He has won no fame and holds no rank, and he goes looking for a sword only because his brother Sir Kay's has broken at a tournament.

The first part, The Book of King Arthur, follows him as he wins his crown, the sword Excalibur and a queen, the Lady Guinevere. The second, The Book of Three Worthies, tells three longer stories: of Merlin, of Sir Pellias and of Sir Gawaine, full of quests, enchantments and tests of a knight's word.

Howard Pyle drew on the old Arthurian romances and wrote them in his own old-fashioned voice; this edition puts it into clear modern English. In his foreword he says he hoped readers would see in these knights a picture of courage and humility.

orientation.text: Two books, each with its own foreword or prologue and conclusion, and the stories inside told in numbered chapters. Many chapters open with a short summary, in italics, of what is about to happen.
